reason: Wave 6 stage 1 (about 1 h). No CTL certificate (extracted CTL62 sweep: 235 runs of NG, NG with history and RWL_mod: 181 false, 54 timeouts, no true). The bounce map is now an exact particle picture. The head carries no state between runs. Odd defects drift 2 cells left per bounce. Walls (even runs and 00) are parity flips; only the leftmost one moves, one run right per bounce (324/324), and everything right of it stays frozen. A moving wall annihilates with the next frozen wall. A defect reaching the left edge as a leading 1 is born as a wall. The right-end emitter absorbs arriving walls safely (216/216). Halting chain (scripts/stage1/chain_checks.py): a wall reaching a frozen '1:' (run 1 before a 00) leaves an interior 000 (36/36), and a wall reaching a frozen 000 halts the machine (105/105). Keeping each of those frozen needs a birth at exactly the right bounce. The real run had 11 '1:' episodes to 3e10, all unfrozen, and no interior 000 at any left-end bounce. Changing only when 3 defects reach the left edge makes the real tape at step 1,238,230,449 halt 105 bounces later. Birth timing shows no lock (same-bounce birth and annihilation 14 vs 22.7 expected). So non-halting depends on timing coincidences never lining up: cryptid protocol, flagged and stopped. The birth rate falls from 1.55% to 0.54% of bounces by 3e10; the rough halting estimate ranges from about 1e16 steps to astronomically late. Siblings 248/582 share the route (no 000 to 1e10).
